item.title: Bulikula secure dominant 40–4 win over PNG Orchids
item.description: The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have secured a dominant 40–4 victory over the PNG Orchids in their second international rugby league match today. Fiji made a strong start, scoring early to take control of the match and heading into half-time with a commanding 30–4 lead.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have secured a dominant 40–4 victory over the PNG Orchids in their second international rugby league match today.

Fiji made a strong start, scoring early to take control of the match and heading into half-time with a commanding 30–4 lead.

The Bulikula continued their momentum in the second half, adding two more tries to extend their lead to 40–4.

Sienna Laing and Luisa Yaranamua were among the try-scorers for Fiji, while Taina Naividi also crossed the line.

The Bulikula maintained pressure on the Orchids with strong attacking play and defensive efforts, forcing errors and turnovers throughout the match.

Despite several attempts to build momentum, the PNG Orchids managed only one try in the match, with their conversion unsuccessful.

Tahlia Marshall was awarded Player of the Match after scoring a hat-trick for Fiji.

The Fiji Bulikula will face France Women in Round 3 of the Rugby League World Cup next Saturday at 2.20pm at the Cbus Super Stadium, Gold Coast, Australia.

item.title: Nadi and Nadroga to clash in Skipper Cup grand final next Saturday
item.description: It was an exciting day of rugby, with closely contested matches across the Skipper Cup Senior and Under-20 competitions, as well as the Subrails Marama Championship semi-finals. In the Skipper Cup Senior division, Nadi secured a 26–19 victory over Naitasiri to book their place in the final, while Nadroga edged Tailevu 37–32 in another thrilling encounter.
item.content:encoded:
It was an exciting day of rugby, with closely contested matches across the Skipper Cup Senior and Under-20 competitions, as well as the Subrails Marama Championship semi-finals.

In the Skipper Cup Senior division, Nadi secured a 26–19 victory over Naitasiri to book their place in the final, while Nadroga edged Tailevu 37–32 in another thrilling encounter.

The results set up a Nadi-Nadroga final in the Senior division.

In the Subrails Marama Championship, Namosi edged Nadi 41–39 in a high-scoring semi-final , while Nasinu defeated Suva 38–29 to secure their place in the final.

Meanwhile, the Skipper Cup Under-20 semi-finals also delivered exciting contests, with Nadroga defeating Suva 48–31, while Nadi narrowly beat Ba 18–17.

The 2026 Skipper Cup grand final is scheduled for next Saturday, with the venue and kick-off time yet to be confirmed.

item.content:encoded:
Tailevu Rugby Football Union has raised $1,040 through its Blue Night Fundraising Event to help meet allowances for team officials and cover other operational expenses ahead of this afternoon’s Skipper Cup semi-final.

The Fresh Choice Tailevu Rugby Football Union says the funds will assist the committee in meeting its $100 allowance pledge for team officials, as well as supporting its rugby programmes and ongoing commitments.

The union has thanked supporters, families, friends and well-wishers who attended the fundraising event at Nausori Gym Hall.

Meanwhile, Tailevu will face Nadroga in the Skipper Cup semi-finals at HFC Bank Stadium today, while Nadi will host Naitasiri at King Charles Park.

item.title: Fiji is a sleeping giant with the talent to become a formidable force – Jake White
item.description: Pita Toganivalu , Mikaele Liga · 24/10/2026 FIJI Water Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says Fiji is a sleeping giant, with the team having the talent and potential to become a formidable force if players can bring their individual brilliance together as one team.
item.content:encoded:
Pita Toganivalu , Mikaele Liga · 24/10/2026

FIJI Water Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says Fiji is a sleeping giant, with the team having the talent and potential to become a formidable force if players can bring their individual brilliance together as one team.

White says Fijian players continue to excel in overseas competitions, including the Top 14, Japanese League and English Premiership, where they receive individual recognition through awards such as Most Valuable Player and top try-scorer.

However, he says the challenge is bringing those talented players together and ensuring they perform as a collective when representing Fiji.

White says the goal is to bring the same enthusiasm, energy and high level of performance that players show for their overseas clubs into the Fiji jumper.

He believes Fiji has the talent to become a dangerous team when individual skills and abilities are combined with strong teamwork.

White also highlights the importance of mental toughness, confidence and stability as the team continues to improve .

He says the coaching staff are working closely with the players, providing guidance and attention to detail as they prepare for today's match.

White says the team must continue to improve step by step, build confidence, and work together to achieve the desired results.

He believes Fiji can win if the players perform to their potential, remain mentally strong, and translate their individual talent into a united team performance.

Fiji will face Japan this afternoon at 5.50pm in Tokyo.

item.title: Bulikula chase first World Cup win against PNG Orchids today
item.description: As the Bulikula prepare to take on the Papua New Guinea Orchids in the Women’s Rugby League World Cup today, the Fiji side will be chasing its first win after pushing the Kiwi Ferns close in their opening match last week. Fiji suffered an 18–12 defeat to the Kiwi Ferns at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle, Australia, while PNG opened their campaign with a commanding 58–4 victory over France in f
item.content:encoded:
As the Bulikula prepare to take on the Papua New Guinea Orchids in the Women’s Rugby League World Cup today, the Fiji side will be chasing its first win after pushing the Kiwi Ferns close in their opening match last week.

Fiji suffered an 18–12 defeat to the Kiwi Ferns at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle, Australia, while PNG opened their campaign with a commanding 58–4 victory over France in front of their home crowd.

Despite the loss, Bulikula captain Sereana Naitokatoka says the team was encouraged by its performance against one of the tournament’s top sides.

Naitokatoka says going up against the second best in the world and losing only by one try is crazy.

She says the team would have been smashed by probably 30-plus, but for the girls to turn up every single time and lose by one try is amazing.

However, Fiji will be without Tamika Jones for the remainder of the World Cup after she suffered a shoulder injury against the Kiwi Ferns.

The 23-year-old Australia-based player will return home for surgery rather than travel with the team to Papua New Guinea.

Bulikula coach Jone Wesele says the opening match had given the team valuable experience and a benchmark to build on for the rest of the tournament.

The Bulikula will face the PNG Orchids at 3.15pm today at the Santos National Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

item.title: White wants players to play with confidence and purpose
item.description: Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says his focus is on keeping things simple, building players confidence and improving the team game management ahead of their Test match against Japan this afternoon. White, who has had only five training sessions with the team, says he wants to provide structure and direction while allowing Fiji players to express their natural skills on the field.
item.content:encoded:
Flying Fijians head coach Jake White says his focus is on keeping things simple, building players confidence and improving the team game management ahead of their Test match against Japan this afternoon.

White, who has had only five training sessions with the team, says he wants to provide structure and direction while allowing Fiji players to express their natural skills on the field.

He says coaching some of the best players in the world has been exciting, adding that he believes the team can deliver a strong performance if players apply what they have learnt and go a step further.

White says one of the key areas he wants to improve is Fiji's ability to manage matches, particularly through the decision-making of the half-backs and full-back.

He says Fijian players are naturally inclined to play an expansive style of rugby, but combining that attacking instinct with better game management will help the team control matches and move opponents around the field.

The Flying Fijians will play Japan at 5.50pm today in Tokyo.

item.title: Nadi Rugby gives back to the community ahead of Skipper Cup semi-final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/10/2026 The Nadi Rugby side took some time off from their busy schedule to hand out food to those in need ahead of their Skipper Cup semi-final clash with Naitasiri.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/10/2026

The Nadi Rugby side took some time off from their busy schedule to hand out food to those in need ahead of their Skipper Cup semi-final clash with Naitasiri.

The senior team handed out food parcels and also shared meals with those in need around Nadi.

The club acknowledged the players and everyone who helped prepare and distribute the food.

They say even small acts of kindness can make a difference, and they are grateful for the chance to serve their community.

Last week, the club donated essential items to the Treasure House Orphanage in Legalega.

Nadi will be looking to upset the Highlanders, but they know they will need to put in the hard yards to qualify for the final.

Meanwhile, Nadi have named their 23-member squad, with former Swire Shipping Fijian Drua captain Meli Derenalagi starting at number 8, Ebenzer Tuidraki at flanker, and former Fiji 7s representative Kitione Taliga at flyhalf.

Nadi captain Peni Naruma has sent his best wishes to his teammates as he prepares to make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians in Japan tomorrow.

Looking at the Skipper Cup semi-finals, Nadi will face Naitasiri at King Charles Park, while Tailevu will host Nadroga at the HFC Bank Stadium.

Both semi-finals will kick off at 3pm tomorrow.

In the Subrails Marama Cup semi-finals, Nadi will face Namosi at King Charles Park, while Nasinu will take on Suva at the HFC Bank Stadium.

The Marama Cup semi-finals will kick off at 1pm tomorrow.

In the U20 semi-finals, Suva will host Nadroga at the HFC Bank Stadium, while Nadi will meet Ba at King Charles Park.

Both U20 semi-finals will kick off at 11am tomorrow.
